# Generate the layout

Choose **one** of the three examples below, change its numbers to your trial, and run it. The other two boxes stay switched off (`eval = FALSE`). Use your own entries from `data/entries_template.csv` (replace the example names with yours).

```{r entries}
entries <- read.csv("data/entries_template.csv")
head(entries)
nrow(entries)
```

**Option A: alpha-lattice** (100 or fewer entries in a normal yield trial, 2 or more replicates)

```{r alpha, eval = TRUE}
# HINT: t = number of entries (30 in the template), k = plots per block (t must be divisible by k: 3, 5, 6 or 10), r = replicates
design <- alpha_lattice(t = nrow(entries), k = ___, r = ___, seed = 2026, data = entries)   # TODO
head(design$fieldBook)
plot(design)
```

**Option B: augmented** (many lines, one plot each, checks repeated)

```{r augmented, eval = FALSE}
# HINT: nrows x ncols must be at least lines + checks (and repeated checks)
design <- diagonal_arrangement(nrows = 20, ncols = 25, lines = 460, checks = 4, seed = 2026)
head(design$fieldBook)
plot(design)
```

**Option C: p-rep** (a fraction of the lines in two plots)

```{r prep, eval = FALSE}
design <- partially_replicated(nrows = 20, ncols = 25, repGens = c(40, 420),
                               repUnits = c(2, 1), seed = 2026)
head(design$fieldBook)
plot(design)
```

# Export the field book

```{r export}
# Always keep the row and the column (or block) of every plot
write.csv(design$fieldBook, "my_field_book.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
